pitch_detail.notes: East Eagle Trail #1910 runs about 1.5 mi up the valley floor before the route leaves it to the right. The trailhead has a self-issue wilderness permit station; fill one out before starting.
Steep, loose rib between two drainages on the west side. Exposure and big loose blocks; the crux of the day.
Cross the crest between the two tops of the double summit; the east summit is the higher.

After the east summit the route keeps to the crest, then drops rubbly, loose slopes to Crater Lake. The lake is a dammed reservoir with campsites along its north shore; the trail is picked up near the outlet by the dam.
pitch_detail.pitch: Crest and descent to Crater Lake

pitch_detail.notes: Little Kettle Creek Trail runs down a steep, open north-facing slope in more than 25 switchbacks, with little shade. It crosses rocky gullies and small creeks, passes a pika talus slope, is lightly used and can be overgrown or rough in places.

review.changed: Wrote all three thin boxes. Trail descent details come from the same trail described in the uphill direction (switchbacks, open slope, creeks, overgrowth). Crater Lake box adds only the dam/campsite facts; no crest distance or terrain was stated anywhere so none invented. No lengths given.
review.other_findings: FKT page calls the return the Kettle Creek Trail; the stored Little Kettle Creek #1945 matches the Forest Service trail name.

pitch_detail.notes: Arapaho Pass trail to the mine ruins, Arapaho Glacier trail to the saddle, then a loose rocky scramble past a false summit to the top.
Leave South Arapaho northward; an exposed downclimb of about 50 ft, then sustained blocky scrambling. Stay near the crest, escape west at difficulties.
About three quarters of the way along: two short steps of roughly 8-10 ft each on good holds, above exposure.

Past the hard steps, work along the east side of the crest, then climb through large boulders to the broad, fairly flat summit with a big cairn. Cairns mark the last stretch and the line is easy to lose; backtrack rather than force it.

Reverse the ridge back to South Arapaho, downclimbing the crux steps; allow roughly an hour. The ridge stays around 13,500 ft for a long stretch, so start early and watch for afternoon storms. The rock is mostly sound, with some rotten sections.
Scramble off South Arapaho to the saddle, then follow the Arapaho Glacier trail and the Arapaho Pass trail back down past the mine ruins.

review.changed: Wrote the three thin boxes from the three pages. Old Baldy is described on one page as a 15-min walk from the saddle east of South Arapaho. Left out lengths (none firm).
review.other_findings: One page says orange paint arrows mark the ridge; stored beta says marks are sparse. One page puts the trailhead to mine ruins at ~1.6 mi, stored row says ~2 mi.
